descripcion_es: How to report what someone else said: changes to verb tenses, pronouns and references; say versus tell.
resumen: To report what someone said, use said or told + (that) + the sentence, usually moving the verb tense one step back and adapting pronouns and expressions of time and place.

filas: Past simple: He said (that) he worked there.
Past continuous: She said she was leaving.
Past perfect: He said he had finished.
would: She said she would call me.
could: He said he could swim.
the next day / the following day
the day before / the previous day

items: Say is not followed by a person: He said (that)…; if you want to say who to, say to me. Tell always takes a person: He told me (that)…
That is optional: She said she was tired.
If what was said is still true or the reporting verb is in the present, the tense may not change: He says he is tired; She said Madrid is the capital of Spain.

ejemplos.frase: “I'm hungry,” said Leo. → Leo said he was hungry.
ejemplos.traduccion: «Tengo hambre», dijo Leo. → Leo dijo que tenía hambre.

ejemplos.frase: She told me she had lost her phone.
ejemplos.traduccion: Me dijo que había perdido el móvil.

ejemplos.frase: They said they would come the next day.
ejemplos.traduccion: Dijeron que vendrían al día siguiente.

ejemplos.frase: My boss told us the meeting was cancelled.
ejemplos.traduccion: Mi jefa nos dijo que la reunión se había cancelado.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: She said me that she was tired.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: She told me that she was tired.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: With a person after the verb, use tell; say cannot take “me” directly.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: He told that he was busy.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: He said that he was busy.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Tell needs the person you are speaking to; without it, use say.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: He said he will help me.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: He said he would help me.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: With a reporting verb in the past, will normally becomes would (just as in Spanish “dijo que me ayudaría”).

ejercicios.frase: She ___ me that she was moving to Valencia.
respuestas: told
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule from the rules and key points applies: tell always takes the person spoken to, whereas say is not followed by a person. The clue is me immediately after the gap: with a person as object, the verb is told. The rest of the sentence is already in reported speech (was moving, past continuous).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: With a person (me) after it: told.
ejercicios.traduccion: Me dijo que se mudaba a Valencia.

por_opcion.said: Incorrect: said cannot be followed directly by the person; you would need said to me or, better, told me.
por_opcion.told: Correct: told + person (me) + (that) + clause is the reported speech structure with tell.
por_opcion.spoke: Incorrect: speak means to talk and does not introduce what is said with that; also, “spoke me” is not grammatical (spoke to me).

ejercicios.frase: He ___ that the shop was closed.
respuestas: said
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the rule that complements the previous one: with no person after the verb, use say. The clue is that that comes straight after the gap, with no me, him or us. That is why only said is possible; told would require mentioning who was told.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: With no person after it: said.
ejercicios.traduccion: Dijo que la tienda estaba cerrada.

por_opcion.said: Correct: said + (that) + clause, with no person after it.
por_opcion.told: Incorrect: told needs the person (told me that…); “He told that” is the typical mistake listed on the card.
por_opcion.told to: Incorrect: told to is followed by an infinitive to give orders (he told me to wait), and the person is missing too.

ejercicios.frase: “I can't come.” → She said she ___ come.
respuestas: couldn't
ejercicios.explicacion: The tense table applies: can becomes could in reported speech. The clue is the reporting verb in the past (said), which moves the tense of what was said back. The negative stays, so can't becomes couldn't, just as in Spanish “no puedo” becomes “no podía”.
ejercicios.traduccion: «No puedo venir.» → Dijo que no podía venir.

por_opcion.can't: Incorrect in this exercise: with said the normal choice is to move back to couldn't; can't would only stay if the impossibility were still true now and you wanted to stress it.
por_opcion.couldn't: Correct: can't → couldn't when changing to reported speech after said.
por_opcion.won't: Incorrect: won't is the future form will not and changes the meaning (he will refuse or will not come); also, in reported speech it would be wouldn't.

ejercicios.enunciado: Choose the correct option (you are reporting it a week later).
ejercicios.frase: “I'll see you tomorrow.” → He said he would see me ___.
respuestas: the next day
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the second table in the rules and key points: tomorrow becomes the next day (or the following day) in reported speech. The clue is the instruction: you are reporting it a week later, so “tomorrow” is no longer tomorrow from your point of view. Also, will has become would, which confirms the shift back to the past.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Tomorrow becomes the next day when you report it later.
ejercicios.traduccion: «Te veré mañana.» → Dijo que me vería al día siguiente.

por_opcion.tomorrow: Incorrect: keeping tomorrow only makes sense if you report it on the same day it was said; a week later the day has already passed.
por_opcion.the next day: Correct: tomorrow → the next day when the time reference point changes.
por_opcion.the day before: Incorrect: the day before is the change for yesterday, not for tomorrow.

ejercicios.frase: “I live in Bilbao.” → Ana said she ___ in Bilbao.
respuestas: lived
lives
ejercicios.explicacion: The tense table applies: the present simple becomes the past simple (live → lived). The clue is the reporting verb said, in the past. The card also accepts lives because, according to the last rule in the rules and key points, if what was said is still true the tense may not change: if Ana still lives in Bilbao, “she said she lives in Bilbao” is correct.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Present simple → past simple (lives is also possible if she still lives there).
ejercicios.traduccion: «Vivo en Bilbao.» → Ana dijo que vivía (vive) en Bilbao.

errores_previstos.respuesta: live
errores_previstos.explicacion: With she the present simple takes -s (lives) and, with the usual shift back, the past is lived.

errores_previstos.respuesta: was living
errores_previstos.explicacion: The present simple moves back to the past simple (lived), not to the past continuous.

errores_previstos.respuesta: has lived
errores_previstos.explicacion: The present perfect is not the change for the present simple; the right form is lived (or lives if it is still true).

ejercicios.frase: “We are watching TV.” → They said they ___ TV.
respuestas: were watching
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the row in the table “present continuous → past continuous”. The clue is are watching in the original and the reporting verb said: are becomes were and watching stays. The pronoun we has also changed to they because someone else is now reporting it.
ejercicios.traduccion: «Estamos viendo la tele.» → Dijeron que estaban viendo la tele.

errores_previstos.respuesta: are watching
errores_previstos.explicacion: With said in the past, the present continuous moves back to the past continuous: were watching.

errores_previstos.respuesta: was watching
errores_previstos.explicacion: The subject is they, plural: the auxiliary is were, not was.

errores_previstos.respuesta: watched
errores_previstos.explicacion: The original is continuous and reported speech keeps the aspect: were watching.

ejercicios.frase: “I have finished the project.” → He said he ___ the project.
respuestas: had finished
'd finished
ejercicios.explicacion: The row in the table “present perfect → past perfect” applies. The clue is have finished in the original and said in the introduction: have becomes had. The contraction 'd finished, common in speech, is also accepted. Spanish follows the same pattern (“he terminado” → “había terminado”).
ejercicios.traduccion: «He terminado el proyecto.» → Dijo que había terminado el proyecto.

errores_previstos.respuesta: has finished
errores_previstos.explicacion: This keeps the present perfect; with said in the past it moves back to the past perfect: had finished.

errores_previstos.respuesta: finished
errores_previstos.explicacion: It is possible in relaxed speech, but the rule on the card requires the past perfect: had finished.

errores_previstos.respuesta: had finish
errores_previstos.explicacion: After had you need the past participle: finished.

ejercicios.frase: The teacher ___ us that the exam was on Friday.
respuestas: told
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the say/tell rule: with a person after the verb, use tell. The clue is us right after the gap: the teacher is addressing specific listeners, so the verb is told. Said us would be a word-for-word copy of Spanish “nos dijo”.
ejercicios.traduccion: El profesor nos dijo que el examen era el viernes.

errores_previstos.respuesta: said
errores_previstos.explicacion: Said cannot take the person directly after it; with us you have to use told (or said to us).

errores_previstos.respuesta: tell
errores_previstos.explicacion: The sentence is in the past (was on Friday): you need told.

errores_previstos.respuesta: told to
errores_previstos.explicacion: Tell does not take to before the person: told us.

ejercicios.frase: He said me that he was ill.
respuestas: He told me that he was ill.
He told me he was ill.
He said to me that he was ill.
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule from the rules and key points applies: say is not followed by a person; if you want to say who to, say to me. The clue is me after said, which is the typical mistake on the card (a word-for-word copy of Spanish “me dijo”). There are three valid corrections: change to told me (with or without that) or keep said and add to: said to me.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Say is not followed directly by a person: told me or said to me.

errores_previstos.respuesta: He said me that he was ill.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: say cannot take the person directly after it.

errores_previstos.respuesta: He told to me that he was ill.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Tell does not take to before the person: told me.

errores_previstos.respuesta: He said that he was ill to me.
errores_previstos.explicacion: To me cannot go at the end, after the clause: it goes right after said (said to me that…).

ejercicios.frase: Maria told that she liked the film.
respuestas: Maria said that she liked the film.
Maria said she liked the film.
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the complementary rule: tell needs the person you are speaking to; without it, use say. The clue is that that comes straight after told, with no person as object. The correction is said, with or without that. The tense liked is already correct: it is the present like moved back.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: With no person after the verb, use said.
ejercicios.traduccion: María dijo que le había gustado la película.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Maria told that she liked the film.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: tell needs the person spoken to.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Maria said me that she liked the film.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It has been changed to said, but the person has been added directly after it, which say does not allow.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Maria told she liked the film.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Removing that does not fix anything: tell still has no person.

ejercicios.enunciado: Change into reported speech, starting with “She said”.
respuestas: She said she was very tired.
She said that she was very tired.
ejercicios.explicacion: Two changes from the card apply: the pronoun (I → she, because someone else is now speaking) and the tense (present am → past was), following the table of tense shifts. The clue is the reporting verb in the past, She said. That is optional, so both versions are accepted.

errores_previstos.respuesta: She said she is very tired.
errores_previstos.explicacion: With said in the past, the normal choice is to move back: am → was. Keeping is would only work if you want to stress that she is still tired now.

errores_previstos.respuesta: She said I was very tired.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The pronoun has not been changed: I becomes she, because the person reporting is not the person who said it.

errores_previstos.respuesta: She said me she was very tired.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Say is not followed by a person; also, the instruction asks you to start with She said.

ejercicios.enunciado: Change into reported speech, starting with “Tom said” (you are reporting it days later).
respuestas: Tom said he would call me that night.
Tom said that he would call me that night.
Tom said he'd call me that night.
Tom said that he'd call me that night.
ejercicios.explicacion: Three rules from the card apply: will becomes would (tense table), the pronoun you becomes me (because I am the person addressed) and tonight becomes that night (table of time expressions). The clue is the instruction: you are reporting it days later, so “tonight” is no longer tonight. Versions with and without that and with the contraction he'd are accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Will → would; you → me; tonight → that night.
ejercicios.traduccion: Tom dijo que me llamaría esa noche.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Tom said he will call me tonight.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Neither the tense (will → would) nor the time expression (tonight → that night) has been moved back, which is necessary because you are reporting it days later.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Tom said he would call you that night.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The pronoun has not been changed: you in the original refers to me, so it becomes me.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Tom said he would call me tonight.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The verb tense is correct, but tonight must become that night because you are reporting it days later.

respuestas: she told me she was busy
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the structure on the card: told + person + (that) + clause with the tense moved back. The order is subject (she), told, the person addressed (me) and then the subordinate clause (she was busy). That is optional and is not among the words here.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Told + person + (that) + sentence with the tense moved back.

errores_previstos.respuesta: she told she was busy me
errores_previstos.explicacion: The person goes immediately after told, not at the end of the sentence.

errores_previstos.respuesta: she was busy she told me
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is an inversion typical of direct speech or an aside; in reported speech the reporting verb goes first.

respuestas: they said they had lost the keys
ejercicios.explicacion: The structure said + clause and the shift of tenses apply: what in direct speech would be “We lost / have lost the keys” becomes past perfect, had lost. The order is subject, said, and the complete subordinate clause with subject, had, past participle and object.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Said + sentence in the past perfect.
ejercicios.traduccion: Dijeron que habían perdido las llaves.

errores_previstos.respuesta: they said they lost had the keys
errores_previstos.explicacion: The auxiliary had goes before the past participle: had lost.

errores_previstos.respuesta: they had said they lost the keys
errores_previstos.explicacion: The tense of the reporting verb has been changed instead of the tense in the clause; what is required is said + had lost.

descripcion_larga_es: Reported speech is used to report what someone else said without quoting them word for word: “She said she was tired”. In English it is introduced by said or told, and usually the verb tense moves one step back and pronouns and time expressions change. It is essential for summarising conversations or meetings, and Spanish speakers find it hardest to tell say and tell apart.

contexto.que_es: It is the way of reproducing what someone said by building it into our own sentence, with a reporting verb (say, tell) and a subordinate clause, with or without that. As the point of view changes, verb tenses (usually one step towards the past), pronouns and references to time and place are adapted.
contexto.por_que_importa: Reporting what others have said is one of the most frequent tasks in communication: passing on a message, summarising a meeting or reporting a statement. A mistake with say and tell or with the verb tense does not stop people understanding the sentence, but it is very noticeable and is among the most heavily penalised in an exam. Also, forgetting to change the tense can suggest that what was said is still true today.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: It is used when passing on a message, telling someone about a past conversation, or summarising statements in a report or a news item. The signal is a reporting verb (said, told) followed by what someone expressed. Spanish also moves the tense back (“dijo que vendría”), which helps; the main difficulty is that say cannot take the person directly (not “said me”) and that tell always requires it.
